newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa sees $80 million layoff charge for restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Televisa sees $80 million layoff charge for restructuring.

text.p: Mexican television company Grupo Televisa SA de CV said Wednesday it will take one-time charges of about $80 million for layoffs in a massive restructuring aimed at cutting costs by $270 million over the next three years.
The company did not specify how many jobs would be lost, but said the charges related to severance and termination costs of senior executives and their staffs.
Televisa said it plans to slash its total debt of $988 million by $100 million in the restructuring.

"Through a combination of the strengthening Mexican economy, cost-cutting measures and efforts to increase revenues, the company expects its cash flow margins to exceed 25 percent," CEO Guillermo Canedo White said.
Televisa's American Depositary Receipts rose $1.375 to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
"We saw this coming for the last few days, and it looks like it should be good for the company," said one trader.
Televisa was scheduled to meet with shareholders and analysts in New York Wednesday to outline the company's strategy and vision after patriarch Emilio Azcarraga Milmo's recent death.

The company, based in Mexico City, said it plans to "freeze certain executive salaries and reduce overtime salaries." A new, performance-based compensation policy of issuing stock options and other executive benefits in place of salary increases.
In addition, Televisa is looking to cut real estate rental expenses and promotional expenses for records and publishing, it said.
